title: Frontend's transporter type question is headed "What type of transporter will move the animals?" and offers Commercial then Private, each explained; Design release 1 heads it "Choose a transporter type", warns the trader to search first, puts Private first and explains only Commercial

finding.frontend: The type question is headed "What type of transporter will move the animals?" as the page's h1 inside the fieldset legend, hinted "We will ask for the transporter's details next.", with no caption above it and no warning. It offers two radios in this order: Commercial, hinted "A business approved to transport animals — you will choose one from a list", then Private, hinted "You or another individual moving the animals — you will give their address". The copy is at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:60-61 and the captured DOM of fe-transporter-type carries all of it verbatim. The page a trader reaches by answering Private is headed "Private transporter details" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:99), again with no caption.
finding.prototype: Design release 1 heads the same question "Choose a transporter type" under a caption reading "Add a new transporter", and puts a warning between the heading and the radios: "Before you add this transporter, please ensure you have already searched for it first." (app/views/transporter-add.html:31-36). The fieldset legend is visually hidden, so the heading does the work. The radios are the other way round — Private transporter first with no hint at all, then Commercial with one hint, "This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland." — and the labels differ too: "Private transporter" rather than "Private". The page reached by answering Private is headed "Add private transporter" under the same "Add a new transporter" caption (app/views/transporter-add-private.html:30-31).
finding.difference: Rewrite the type question's copy to match Design release 1 and rename the private form's heading with it. On the type page: change the heading to "Choose a transporter type", add the caption "Add a new transporter" above it, add a warning reading "Before you add this transporter, please ensure you have already searched for it first.", drop the "We will ask for the transporter's details next." hint, reverse the two options so Private transporter comes first, relabel Private as "Private transporter", drop both of the frontend's explanatory hints and give Commercial the single hint "This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland." All of that is src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:60-61 and the template that reads it. On the private form: change the heading at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:99 from "Private transporter details" to "Add private transporter" and add the same "Add a new transporter" caption. This is copy on two pages Frontend already has and the band is frontend-work. It is independently schedulable from transport--transporter-type-asked-before-any-list, which moves the type question off the linear journey and onto an add route: the copy can be corrected on the page where it stands today, and the flow can be restructured without any of the copy changing. Note one thing for whoever schedules them together — Design release 1's warning tells the trader to search first, which only makes sense once the searchable list that flow change introduces exists, so if the copy lands alone the warning is the one sentence that will read oddly until it does.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding the heading "Choose a transporter type", the caption "Add a new transporter", or Private above Commercial in the captured DOM of fe-transporter-type. That file has one h1 reading "What type of transporter will move the animals?", no caption element, and Commercial as the first of two radios.
finding.verification: No independent verifier: this finding was split out of transport--transporter-type-asked-before-any-list by the corpus editor during a pre-ingest edit pass, and no second agent has verified it in its own right. It inherits a verification of the same copy, written by an agent other than that finding's author, which checked capture/html/prototype/dr1-transporter-add.html and confirmed the caption, the heading, the warning sentence, the reversed radio order and the single Commercial hint are all as quoted. The editor read both sides again line by line while splitting, because this file makes the copy the whole substance rather than a clause inside a flow change, and every string above was taken from a rendered file or a source file rather than from the parent finding's prose: the frontend heading, hint, order and both radio hints from capture/html/frontend/fe-transporter-type.html:135-160 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:60-61; the frontend private heading from capture/html/frontend/fe-transporter-private.html:117; the Design release 1 caption, heading and warning from app/views/transporter-add.html:31-36 with the rendered form at capture/html/prototype/dr1-transporter-add.html:234-239; the reversed radios, the "Private transporter" label and the Commercial hint from capture/html/prototype/dr1-transporter-add.html:257-276; and the private form heading from app/views/transporter-add-private.html:30-31. Two things the editor checked that the parent finding did not state and that this one now does: Design release 1's Private option carries no hint at all, and its fieldset legend is visually hidden so the h1 above it is what a trader reads. Both citations are root views, not release subfolders.
finding.correction: Not a correction of a claim — a record of provenance, because this file did not exist when the slice was verified. It was split from transport--transporter-type-asked-before-any-list, a flow-change finding that had already spun three children off and still carried, inside its difference slot, the type chooser's new heading, its warning text, its reversed option order, its rewritten hints and the private form's heading rename. Those are copy edits to two pages that exist today and they need no flow change to land, so under the contract's rule that a sentence containing "and also" is two findings they are now separate files. The parent keeps the flow — one combined searchable list first, the type question moved onto an add route off it — and this file takes the words. Nothing in either file's claims changed in the split; the strings were re-read from the captured DOM rather than copied across.

relatedTo.why: This finding was split from that one. That one moves the type question off the linear journey onto an add route behind a combined transporter list; this one is the words on the question itself and on the private form it leads to. Either can land without the other, but Design release 1's warning to search first only reads sensibly once that list exists.
